title: Do electric cars actually help?

turns.speaker: Chris
turns.text: My brother-in-law keeps telling me the electric car is worse for the planet because of the battery. Every single time I see him.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: It's worse to build. That part's true. Making the battery puts you in debt before you've driven anywhere.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Depends almost entirely on the grid you charge from. Somewhere with a lot of coal, maybe fifty or sixty thousand miles. Somewhere mostly renewable, it can be under fifteen.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: It is, and it's the whole argument. People quote whichever end suits them.

turns.speaker: Ian
turns.text: There's a second thing that bothers me, which is that it's still a car. Two tonnes of metal to move one person to work. We're solving the fuel and keeping the traffic.

turns.speaker: Chris
turns.text: And the tyre dust, apparently. Which is worse, because they're heavier.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: That's right, and it's the part nobody legislates because it doesn't come out of a pipe.

turns.speaker: Ian
turns.text: So the honest position is, better than petrol, nowhere near as good as not driving.

turns.speaker: Chris
turns.text: I'm going to say that to him and he's going to hear the first half only.

turns.speaker: Ian
turns.text: Everyone does. That's why the argument never ends.

points: Building an electric car has a higher carbon cost than a petrol one, chiefly because of the battery.
The break-even distance depends mainly on the electricity grid: roughly fifty to sixty thousand miles on a coal-heavy grid, under fifteen thousand on a largely renewable one.
Maya notes the wide range is why both sides can quote a figure that suits them.
Ian's second objection is that an electric car is still a car, so congestion and the mass moved per person are unchanged.
Heavier vehicles produce more tyre particulates, which are not regulated because they are not tailpipe emissions.
Their agreed position is that electric cars are better than petrol but far worse than not driving.
